We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1.

The guidance: three steps: (1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). (2) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated acid (C=C) from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. (3) sulfonamide formation from amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthetic direction: target -> break amide bond to give acid and aniline (or amine). The amide is C(=O)N attached to aromatic ring (anilide). The amide is attached to the α,β-unsaturated chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-... So the amide carbonyl is part of the chain: C(=O)N attached to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So step 1: disconnect amide to give α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (with C=C) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The acid is something like: /C=C/C(=O)OH attached to aromatic ring? Actually the product after breaking amide: we get the acid: /C=C/C(=O)OH attached to aromatic ring? The chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2? Wait the target: .../C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N. So the amide carbonyl attached to N which is attached to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So the amide is between the α,β-unsaturated acid and an aniline (anilide). So retrosynthesis: acid = /C=C/C(=O)OH attached to aromatic ring (the phenyl sulfonyl part). Actually the acid is attached to the phenyl sulfonyl group via the aromatic ring? The chain: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the α,β-unsaturated amide is attached to the second phenyl ring (c2). So the acid precursor would be the same phenyl ring with the α,β-unsaturated acid (c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)OH)cc2). Then amide formation with aniline (c3ccccc3N). Good.

Step 2: The α,β-unsaturated acid can be formed via Doebner modification from an aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(C=O)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). The Doebner yields α,β-unsaturated acid attached to the aromatic ring: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)OH)cc2. So we need aldehyde precursor: p-tolyl? Actually the aromatic ring is substituted with the sulfonamide group at para position relative to the chain? The target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. So the first phenyl (c1) has a methyl (C) and sulfonamide linking to second phenyl (c2). The second phenyl has the α,β-unsaturated amide side chain at para position relative to sulfonyl? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the aldehyde precursor would be c2ccc(C=O)cc2 (para-aldehyde). So step 2: aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid.

Step 3: sulfonamide formation: combine sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) with aniline (the first phenyl with methyl) to give sulfonamide linking the two phenyls. The sulfonyl chloride derived from the second phenyl? Actually the sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O) attached to the first phenyl (with methyl) and to the second phenyl (the sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl). The sulfonyl chloride would be derived from the second phenyl (c2) bearing sulfonyl chloride at para position relative to the side chain? The SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor: c2ccc(Cl)cc2 (para-chlorosulfonyl? Actually sulfonyl chloride is -SO2Cl attached to aromatic ring. So the precursor is aromatic sulfonyl chloride: c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2. Then react with aniline (c1 with methyl) to give sulfonamide.

Thus overall retrosynthesis:

Target (T) -> disconnection 1 (amide): gives precursor A: aromatic sulfonamide phenyl with α,β-unsaturated acid (c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)OH)cc2) attached to sulfonyl phenyl (via sulfonamide). plus aniline (c3ccccc3N). Actually the sulfonamide remains attached to first phenyl; the amide disconnection does not affect sulfonamide. So after step 1, we have intermediate I1: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)OH)cc2)cc1 (the acid version) and aniline.

Step 2: I1 -> disconnection 2 (Doebner): break α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid. So precursor I2: aromatic aldehyde c2ccc(C=O)cc2 attached to sulfonamide phenyl (same sulfonamide). plus malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). (Malonic acid is a simple reagent, not needed to be listed as a node maybe). So I2 is Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1.

Step 3: I2 -> disconnection 3 (sulfonamide formation): break sulfonamide to sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl and aniline (first phenyl with methyl). So precursors: aniline (c1 with methyl) = Cc1ccc(NH2)cc1 and sulfonyl chloride: c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2 (attached to the aldehyde? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is on the second phenyl, which also has aldehyde at para position. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor is Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1? Wait the first phenyl is methyl-substituted; the second phenyl is not methyl. The sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second phenyl which also has aldehyde. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor is c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2 with aldehyde at para? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is at para position relative to aldehyde? In target, the sulfonamide attaches at para position to the side chain? The SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/... )cc2. So the sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl at the position where the side chain is attached? Wait the sulfonamide attaches to the phenyl at the same carbon as the side chain? The SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/... )cc2. The sulfonamide is attached to the phenyl at the same carbon as the side chain? Actually the SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/... )cc2 means the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl carbon (c2) which also has the side chain substituent at another position (para). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2 with aldehyde at para? The aldehyde is at the position where side chain will be after Doebner. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor is Cc1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1? No methyl is on first phenyl, not second. So second phenyl has no methyl. So sulfonyl chloride precursor: c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2 with aldehyde at para: c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2 where the aldehyde is at para? Actually we need both functionalities on same phenyl: aldehyde and sulfonyl chloride. So the precursor is c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2 with an aldehyde at para position: c2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2 where the aldehyde is at the position that will become side chain after Doebner. So the SMILES: O= Cc2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2 (para-aldehyde sulfonyl chloride). That is a known reagent.

Thus final retrosynthesis route: three reactions:

1. Amide coupling: acid (I1) + aniline (c3ccccc3N) -> target.

2. Doebner modification: aldehyde (c2ccc(C=O)cc2) + malonic acid -> I1 (acid).

3. Sulfonamide formation: aniline (Cc1ccc(NH2)cc1) + aromatic sulfonyl chloride (O= Cc2ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc2) -> I2 (aldehyde sulfonyl phenyl).

We need to provide JSON route with nested reactions.

We need template IDs for each reaction. We can search for templates matching each transformation.

First, amide coupling (carboxylic acid + amine -> amide). Use search with functional_groups_broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid, functional_groups_formed: amide. Already we got template ID 401931 (retro_smarts). That template seems to be for amide formation with α,β-unsaturated acid? It includes C-C double bond etc. But we can use it.
